_: THE CLOSED LIST of SecurityInsight's guards (#277): SWITCHES (#414): every guard can be turned off (SI_Guard_<Token>_Enabled, its mail SI_Guard_<Token>_Mail, all at once SI_Guards_Enabled; Settings > Guards) -- 'whenOff' says, in plain words, what turning it off means. RELEASING (framework GUARD-1.6, #404): only the kinds release-held-set and release-collection can be released -- by a SuperAdmin, with a reason, once (one run, or until a time of at most 24 hours), bound to the held plan's hash; every other guard carries 'neverReleasable': the reason, in plain words, it can never be released (the data is wrong, nothing is held, it would write where the customer did not allow it, or it protects integrity). every place where SecurityInsight holds, refuses or halts a step to protect data. Read by BOTH writers of a guard event: PowerShell (engine/_shared/SI-Guard.ps1, Send-SIGuardEvent) and the Pro web app (SI.Management.Web Guards/GuardEvents.cs, linked into the build). A test compares the two readers and checks every Send-SIGuardEvent call names a guard listed here. An id is stable and dotted (area.object.what): adding one = one entry here; renaming one breaks the history of the old id -- add, never rename. 'protects' and 'action' are the words a customer reads in the mail: plain language, no internal numbers. THE THREE PARTS a person reads on the Guards page, in the mail and (without detail) in the report to Invardia: 'what' (what happened, one sentence), 'why' (the cause of THIS event), 'consequence' (what the user sees or misses; 'nothing is lost' where it holds) and 'steps' (what to do, short). Placeholders, filled from the event: {held} (what was held), {v:<value name>} (a measured value), {detail}, {subject}, {when}, {latest} (the web app only: the newest collection it shows); {name|text} uses text when the value is empty; a [ ... ] part is left out when a placeholder in it is empty. 'what', 'consequence' and 'steps' never use {detail} or {subject} (they travel to Invardia). 'kind' says what a release means for the guard: release-held-set (an Admin releases the held set once), release-collection (an Admin loads a held collection once, marked partial), fix-source (cannot be released: fix the cause), next-run (resolved by the next successful run), rerun (re-run the job), setting (change a setting or the licence), review (check the result), info (nothing to do). Every event can be acknowledged. THE FOUR TEXTS of the Guards page (operator 2026-10-09: nobody understood the guards): 'name' (a short plain name), 'what' (what happened), 'why' (why it held: what it protects you from, then the run's own words), 'ifRelease' (what a release does -- or, for a guard that cannot be released, why not and what to do instead) and 'consequence' (if you leave it), plus 'steps'. 'limits' names the settings that tune a guard (edited on the Guards page under Control) and 'limitsInfo' says what changing them means.

guards.name: Vulnerability close limit
guards.protects: open vulnerability records
guards.action: SecurityInsight would have closed far more vulnerability records in one run than it allows, so it closed none. Check that the newest Risk Analysis run was complete and that its vulnerability findings look right. If the large drop is real (for example a big patch round), run the vulnerability connector once with a higher close limit (SI_VulnSync_MaxClosePercent; the absolute limit SI_VulnSync_MaxCloseAbsolute is off by default), then set the limit back -- or turn the check off in Settings > Guards.
guards.whenOff: Off: the step goes on as if the check had not tripped -- the vulnerability connector closes every record the run would close, however many; nothing is held for release.
guards.what: SecurityInsight held {held|many} vulnerability close(s): the vulnerability connector would have closed more records in one run than it may close at once.
guards.why: This check stops a broken or incomplete collection from closing many open vulnerabilities in your target by mistake. A big patch round looks the same, so SecurityInsight closes none and lets a person decide. {detail|The newest results no longer report far more of the open findings than usual.}
guards.ifRelease: The held closes go through once: the records are closed in the target with the next run of the connector -- only those that are still absent then, and only after the results are checked as complete. The release is for this held set only and ends by itself.
guards.consequence: Nothing is lost: the records stay open in the target exactly as they were. The held closes are kept for 7 days; after that they expire and the next complete run decides again.
steps: Check that the newest Risk Analysis run finished completely (Operations > Jobs > Run health).
If the drop is real (for example a patch round), a SuperAdmin releases the held closes once with Release in "Held now" at the top of the Guards page.
If your patch rounds often close this many, raise the close limit under Control on the Guards page.
If it is not real, do nothing: the held closes expire after 7 days.
guards.limitsInfo: A higher limit lets more records close in one run without being held: a big patch round goes through by itself, but a broken collection can also close more records before the check stops it.

guards.name: Vulnerabilities: empty result
guards.protects: open vulnerability records
guards.action: The newest Risk Analysis results held no vulnerabilities while records are still open, so nothing was closed. Check that the Risk Analysis Detailed run finished and found vulnerabilities; the next complete run is reconciled as normal.
guards.whenOff: Off: the step goes on as if the check had not tripped -- an EMPTY result closes the open records it no longer reports, so a failed collection can close every open vulnerability.
guards.what: The vulnerability connector closed nothing, because the newest Risk Analysis results held no vulnerabilities at all.
guards.why: This check stops a failed collection from closing every open vulnerability in your target. An empty result almost always means the collection failed, not that everything is fixed. {detail|Records are open in the target, but the newest results report none.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: a release would close every open vulnerability from a result that holds none. The data is wrong, not the limit.
guards.consequence: Nothing is lost: the open records stay open, and the next complete run is handled as normal.
steps: Check that the newest Risk Analysis run finished and found vulnerabilities (Operations > Jobs > Run health).
Nothing else is needed: the next complete run is handled as normal.
guards.neverReleasable: releasing it would close every open vulnerability from a snapshot that holds none -- the data is wrong, not the limit

guards.name: Vulnerabilities: result far smaller than usual
guards.protects: open vulnerability records
guards.action: Far fewer of the open vulnerability records are still reported than usual, which looks like a partial collection rather than a real fix, so nothing was closed. Check the newest Risk Analysis Detailed run and the endpoint data it read; the next complete run is reconciled as normal.
guards.whenOff: Off: the step goes on as if the check had not tripped -- a result that lost most of its findings closes the records it no longer reports.
guards.what: The vulnerability connector closed nothing, because far fewer of the open records are still reported than usual.
guards.why: This check stops a partial collection from closing most of your open vulnerabilities. When most findings disappear at once, the collection is usually broken. {detail|The newest results look like a partial collection, not a real fix.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: a release would close most open vulnerabilities from a result that lost most of its findings.
guards.consequence: Nothing is lost: the open records stay open, and the next complete run is handled as normal.
steps: Check the newest Risk Analysis run and the device data it read (Operations > Jobs > Run health).
Nothing else is needed: the next complete run is handled as normal.
guards.neverReleasable: releasing it would close most open vulnerabilities from a snapshot that lost most of its findings -- a broken run is never a reason to close
guards.limitsInfo: The limit is the share of the open records that must still be reported. A lower share lets runs that report fewer findings close records; a higher share stops more runs. 0 turns the check off.

guards.name: Vulnerabilities: scope changed
guards.protects: open vulnerability records
guards.action: The scope of the collection changed, so records that dropped out of it were not closed. If the narrower scope is intended, close or retire those records in the target yourself.
guards.whenOff: Off: the step goes on as if the check had not tripped -- records that dropped out of the collection scope are closed like any other absent record.
guards.what: Vulnerability records that dropped out of the collection's scope were not closed.
guards.why: This check stops records from being closed only because their assets are no longer collected: a record outside the scope is not fixed, so closing it would report it as fixed. {detail|The scope of the collection changed since the previous run.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: closing what left the scope would report it as fixed. Review the scope instead.
guards.consequence: Nothing is lost: those records stay open in the target, and SecurityInsight no longer updates them.
steps: Check whether the narrower scope is what you want.
If it is, close or retire those records in the target yourself.
If it is not, put the scope back in the settings: the next run picks them up again.
guards.neverReleasable: the set of assets the connector covers changed; closing what left the scope would read as fixed -- review the scope instead

guards.name: Vulnerabilities: Risk Analysis run not finished
guards.protects: open vulnerability records
guards.action: The Risk Analysis run behind these results did not finish cleanly, so nothing was closed. Check the Risk Analysis Detailed run; the next complete run is reconciled as normal.
guards.whenOff: Off: the step goes on as if the check had not tripped -- records are closed even when the Risk Analysis run behind the results did not finish cleanly.
guards.what: The vulnerability connector closed nothing, because the Risk Analysis run behind its results did not finish cleanly.
guards.why: This check stops records from being closed on the strength of a run that did not finish: missing results would look like fixed vulnerabilities. {detail|The Risk Analysis run ended with errors or only partly.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: nothing is ever closed from a run that did not finish.
guards.consequence: Nothing is lost: the open records stay open until a complete run arrives.
steps: Check the Risk Analysis run (Operations > Jobs > Run health).
Nothing else is needed: the next complete run is handled as normal.
guards.neverReleasable: the Risk Analysis run behind the snapshot did not finish; nothing may be closed from an incomplete run

guards.name: Vulnerabilities: results not known to be complete
guards.protects: open vulnerability records
guards.action: The newest Risk Analysis results are not known to be complete, so findings were opened and updated but nothing was closed. Check that the Risk Analysis Detailed run finishes without errors.
guards.whenOff: Off: the step goes on as if the check had not tripped -- absences are counted and records closed even when the newest results are not known to be complete.
guards.what: Vulnerability records were opened and updated, but none was closed.
guards.why: This check stops records from being closed while the newest results are not known to be complete: a missing finding would look like a fixed one. {detail|The newest Risk Analysis results are not known to be complete.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: nothing is ever closed from results that are not known to be complete.
guards.consequence: Nothing is lost: records that would have closed stay open until a complete run confirms they are fixed.
steps: Check that the Risk Analysis run finishes without errors (Operations > Jobs > Run health).
Nothing else is needed: the next complete run closes what is really fixed.
guards.neverReleasable: the snapshot is incomplete; nothing may be closed from an incomplete snapshot

guards.name: Vulnerabilities: target not read in full
guards.protects: your vulnerability target from duplicate records
guards.action: The vulnerability target (for example the ServiceNow table) could not be read in full, so nothing was written: every record the read missed would have been opened again as a duplicate. Check that the target is reachable and the account can read the whole table; the next run tries again.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail. The step itself still stops, because writing after a partial read of the target would open every record the read missed again as a duplicate.
guards.what: The vulnerability connector wrote nothing, because the vulnerability target could not be read in full.
guards.why: This check stops duplicate records: every record the read missed would have been opened again. {detail|Part of the target (for example the ServiceNow table) could not be read.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: writing after a partial read would create duplicates or close the wrong records.
guards.consequence: Nothing is lost and nothing is duplicated: the target is unchanged. This run's new and fixed vulnerabilities reach it with the next run that reads it in full.
steps: Check that the target is reachable and that the account can read the whole table.
Nothing else is needed: the next run tries again.
guards.neverReleasable: the connector could not read the other system completely; closing from a partial read could close the wrong items

guards.name: Vulnerabilities: connector not set up
guards.protects: your vulnerability target
guards.action: A vulnerability connector is not set up completely, so it did not run. Open Configuration > Connectors > Setup in the Pro web app and fix the settings it lists.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail. The step itself still stops, because the connector is not set up completely and cannot run.
guards.what: A vulnerability connector did not run, because it is not set up completely.
guards.why: This check stops a connector from writing to your target with missing or wrong settings. {detail|One or more of its settings are missing or not valid.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: nothing is held. Fix the connector's setup and it runs again.
guards.consequence: Nothing was written to the target. Until the setup is fixed, the target does not receive new or fixed vulnerabilities.
steps: Open Configuration > Connectors > Setup and fix the settings it lists.
The connector runs again on its next schedule.
guards.neverReleasable: the connector definition is not valid (a setting or a secret is missing); there is nothing to release -- fix the definition

guards.name: CMDB table: asset collection not complete
guards.protects: the configuration items (CIs) in your SQL CMDB table
guards.action: The newest asset collection is not known to be complete, so the CMDB table was not changed. Check that the profiling runs (endpoint, Azure) finish without errors; the next complete collection is written as normal.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail. The step itself still stops, because a CI is never written from an asset collection that is not complete.
guards.what: The CMDB table was not changed, because the newest asset collection is not known to be complete.
guards.why: This check stops configuration items from being created, changed or retired from an incomplete collection: a missing asset would look like a retired one. {detail|One of the collection runs (devices, Azure) did not finish cleanly.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: configuration items are never written from an incomplete collection.
guards.consequence: Nothing is lost: the CMDB table keeps its configuration items as they were. New or changed assets reach it with the next complete collection.
steps: Check that the collection runs (devices, Azure) finish without errors (Operations > Jobs > Run health).
Nothing else is needed: the next complete collection is written as normal.
guards.neverReleasable: the profile snapshot is incomplete; CIs are never created, changed or retired from an incomplete snapshot

guards.name: CMDB table: far fewer assets than usual
guards.protects: the configuration items (CIs) in your SQL CMDB table
guards.action: SecurityInsight sees far fewer assets than are active in the CMDB table, which looks like a broken collection rather than assets gone, so nothing was retired. Check the newest profiling runs; the next complete collection is written as normal.
guards.whenOff: Off: the step goes on as if the check had not tripped -- CIs are retired even when SecurityInsight sees far fewer assets than are active in the CMDB table.
guards.what: No configuration item was retired, because SecurityInsight sees far fewer assets than are active in the CMDB table.
guards.why: This check stops a broken collection from retiring healthy configuration items. {detail|The newest collection looks broken rather than the assets being gone.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: retiring from a collection that lost most of its assets would retire healthy configuration items.
guards.consequence: Nothing is lost: every active configuration item stays active until a complete collection confirms it is gone.
steps: Check the newest collection runs (Operations > Jobs > Run health).
Nothing else is needed: the next complete collection is written as normal.
guards.neverReleasable: the snapshot lost most of its assets; retiring CIs from it would retire healthy CIs

guards.name: CMDB table: empty asset collection
guards.protects: the configuration items (CIs) in your SQL CMDB table
guards.action: The newest asset collection holds no assets at all, so nothing was written or retired. Check that the profiling runs collect assets.
guards.whenOff: Off: the step goes on as if the check had not tripped -- an empty asset collection is written too, which can retire every CI.
guards.what: Nothing was written to or retired from the CMDB table, because the newest asset collection holds no assets.
guards.why: This check stops an empty collection from retiring every configuration item. {detail|The collection runs collected no assets.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: a release would retire every configuration item.
guards.consequence: Nothing is lost: the CMDB table is unchanged.
steps: Check that the collection runs collect assets (Operations > Jobs > Run health).
Nothing else is needed: the next collection with assets is written as normal.
guards.neverReleasable: the snapshot is empty; releasing it would retire every CI

guards.name: CMDB table: no correlation results
guards.protects: the configuration items (CIs) in your SQL CMDB table
guards.action: The asset correlation results are missing, so assets could not be matched to their CIs and nothing was written. Run the asset correlation job, then this connector again.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail. The step itself still stops, because without the correlation results no asset can be matched to its CI.
guards.what: Nothing was written to the CMDB table, because the asset correlation results are missing.
guards.why: This check stops assets from being written to the wrong configuration item: without the correlation results, SecurityInsight cannot match them. {detail|The asset correlation results are missing.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: without the correlation results no asset can be matched. Run the correlation job instead.
guards.consequence: Nothing is lost: the CMDB table is unchanged until the correlation results exist.
steps: Run the asset correlation job (Operations > Jobs).
Then run the CMDB connector again, or wait for its next scheduled run.
guards.neverReleasable: without the correlation map CIs cannot be matched to assets; re-run the correlation job instead

guards.name: CMDB table: changed by another run
guards.protects: the configuration items (CIs) in your SQL CMDB table
guards.action: Another run changed the CMDB table while this one was planning, so this run wrote nothing. Nothing is needed if it happens once; if it repeats, make sure the CMDB connector does not run twice at the same time.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail. The step itself still stops, because another run changed the CMDB table meanwhile; the next run plans again.
guards.what: This CMDB run wrote nothing, because another run changed the CMDB table while it was planning.
guards.why: This check stops one run from overwriting what another run just wrote. {detail|Two runs of the CMDB connector overlapped.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: its plan is out of date. The next run plans again from the current table.
guards.consequence: Nothing is lost: the other run's changes stand, and the next run plans again from the current table.
steps: Nothing is needed if it happens once.
If it repeats, make sure the CMDB connector does not run twice at the same time.
guards.neverReleasable: the snapshot is too old to be the truth about the estate; the next fresh run decides

guards.name: CMDB hand-off: large change
guards.protects: the CIs your ServiceNow imports from the CMDB hand-off database
guards.action: Far more of the CIs handed to ServiceNow last time are missing from this run than the connector allows, which looks like a broken collection rather than assets gone, so this run's batch was held and ServiceNow keeps importing the previous one. Check the profiling and correlation runs (for example a lost permission or a failed sign-in). If the change is real, release it once in Operations > Guards (safety checks); otherwise the next run that is back within the limit (the connector's changeGuardPercent) is handed over by itself.
guards.whenOff: Off: the step goes on as if the check had not tripped -- the batch is handed over to ServiceNow however many CIs changed or disappeared.
guards.what: This run's CMDB hand-off batch was held, because far more of the configuration items handed to ServiceNow last time are missing from it than the connector allows.
guards.why: This check stops a broken collection (for example a lost permission or a failed sign-in) from making many configuration items disappear from ServiceNow. {detail|The change looks like a broken collection rather than assets gone.}
guards.ifRelease: The held batch is handed to ServiceNow once: ServiceNow imports it, and the configuration items missing from it are no longer in the hand-off. The release is for this batch only and ends by itself.
guards.consequence: Nothing is lost: ServiceNow keeps importing the previous batch until a run is back within the limit, or the held batch is released.
steps: Check the collection and correlation runs (Operations > Jobs > Run health).
If the change is real, a SuperAdmin releases the batch once with Release in "Held now" at the top of the Guards page.
Otherwise do nothing: the next run that is back within the limit is handed over by itself.
guards.limitsInfo: The allowed change is set on the CMDB hand-off connector (Configuration > Connectors > Setup). A higher limit hands bigger changes to ServiceNow without a hold.

guards.name: ServiceNow: not reachable
guards.protects: the configuration items (CIs) in ServiceNow
guards.action: The ServiceNow instance could not be reached, so nothing was sent. Check the instance address and the account stored for SecurityInsight, and that ServiceNow is up.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail. The step itself still stops, because ServiceNow cannot be reached.
guards.what: Nothing was sent to the ServiceNow CMDB, because the instance could not be reached.
guards.why: This check stops SecurityInsight from sending half a set of changes to ServiceNow. {detail|The ServiceNow instance did not answer, or refused the account.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: ServiceNow cannot be reached, and nothing is held.
guards.consequence: Nothing is lost: ServiceNow keeps its configuration items as they were, and the changes are sent with the next run that reaches it.
steps: Check the instance address and the account stored for SecurityInsight.
Check that ServiceNow is up.
Nothing else is needed: the next run sends the changes.
guards.neverReleasable: ServiceNow could not be reached; there is nothing held to release

guards.name: ServiceNow: create and match rules
guards.protects: the configuration items (CIs) in ServiceNow
guards.action: Some assets were not created or updated in ServiceNow because SecurityInsight could not match them safely (no stable asset id yet, or more than one matching CI). They are listed in the run log; run the asset correlation job with the identity ledger on, and resolve duplicate CIs in ServiceNow.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail. The step itself still stops, because those assets do not meet the connector's create and match rules (set in the connector).
guards.what: {held|Some} asset(s) were not created or updated in ServiceNow, because SecurityInsight could not match them safely.
guards.why: This check stops duplicate or wrong configuration items in ServiceNow: an asset is written only when it matches exactly one configuration item, or when creating is allowed. {detail|They have no stable asset id yet, or more than one configuration item matches them.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: creating configuration items in ServiceNow is a separate switch on the connector, and a release never turns on a write you did not allow.
guards.consequence: The other assets were written. These stay as they were in ServiceNow until they can be matched safely; nothing is lost.
steps: See the run log for the list of assets.
Run the asset correlation job.
Remove duplicate configuration items in ServiceNow.
guards.neverReleasable: creating CIs in ServiceNow is a separate switch (SI_ServiceNow_AllowCreate); a guard release never turns on a write the customer did not allow

guards.name: ServiceNow: service model errors
guards.protects: the placement of assets in your business services
guards.action: The service model has errors, so no asset was placed in a business service. Fix the problems listed in the run log.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail. The step itself still stops, because the service model has errors.
guards.what: No asset was placed in a business service, because the service model has errors.
guards.why: This check stops assets from being placed under the wrong business services. {detail|The service model has problems that must be fixed first.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: a release would place configuration items under the wrong services. Fix the model.
guards.consequence: The placement of assets in your business services stays as it was until the model is fixed.
steps: Fix the problems listed in the run log.
Nothing else is needed: the next run places the assets.
guards.neverReleasable: the service model does not match ServiceNow; fix the model -- a release would write CIs under the wrong services

guards.name: Asset metadata: large change
guards.protects: the asset metadata handed to your CMDB and vulnerability system
guards.action: The full asset metadata collected from one source changed by more than the allowed share since the previous run, which looks like a broken collection rather than a real change, so the previous collection of that source was kept for the hand-off. Check the source (for example a lost permission or a failed sign-in). If the change is real, release it once in Operations > Guards (safety checks); otherwise the next run that is back within the limit (SI_AssetProperties_ChangeGuardPercent) ends the hold by itself.
guards.whenOff: Off: the step goes on as if the check had not tripped -- a large change of the asset metadata is handed over like any other.
guards.what: The asset metadata from one source changed by more than the allowed share since the previous run, so the previous collection of that source is still used for the hand-off.
guards.why: This check stops a broken collection (for example a lost permission or a failed sign-in) from reaching your CMDB and vulnerability system. {detail|The change looks like a broken collection rather than a real change.}
guards.ifRelease: The new collection of that source is handed to your CMDB and vulnerability system once, instead of the previous one. The release is for this run only and ends by itself.
guards.consequence: Nothing is lost: your CMDB and vulnerability system keep receiving the previous collection of that source until a run is back within the limit, or the change is released.
steps: Check the source (for example a lost permission or a failed sign-in).
If the change is real, a SuperAdmin releases it once with Release in "Held now" at the top of the Guards page.
Otherwise do nothing: the next run that is back within the limit ends the hold by itself.
guards.limitsInfo: A higher share lets bigger changes through to your CMDB and vulnerability system without a hold; a lower share holds smaller changes too.

guards.name: Collection: far fewer assets from one source
guards.protects: your configuration items (CIs) and everything calculated from them
guards.action: One source returned far fewer assets than in its last good collection, although the collection completed. That can be a real clean-up (for example many Azure resources removed) or a source that answered only in part, so the assets it no longer lists were kept as they were instead of being marked not seen. Nothing is needed when the drop is real: when the next complete collection of that source shows the same level, it is accepted by itself. To accept such a drop at once instead, set SI_Pro_SourceDropout_AssetDropAction to accept.
guards.whenOff: Off: a collection with far fewer assets is taken as it comes -- the assets the source no longer lists are marked not seen at once, and their CIs retire after the usual days.
guards.what: A source returned far fewer assets than in its last good collection, so the assets it no longer lists were kept as they were.
guards.why: This check stops a source that answered only in part from making healthy assets look gone. {detail|The collection completed, but with far fewer assets than before.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released, and does not need to be: when the next complete collection of that source shows the same level, the drop is accepted by itself.
guards.consequence: Nothing is lost: the run went on, the assets the source no longer lists stay active with their last known data, and no CI is retired and no finding is closed because of the drop. A real clean-up takes effect one run later.
steps: Check the source if the drop is not expected (for example a lost permission, a changed scope or a failed sign-in).
If the drop is real, do nothing: the next complete collection that shows the same level is accepted by itself.
To accept such drops at once from now on, choose accept for this check under Control on the Guards page.
guards.limitsInfo: A higher share lets bigger drops through without keeping the last good collection; a lower share keeps it for smaller drops too. Accept takes every drop as it comes and only reports it.
guards.neverReleasable: nothing waits for a person: the next complete collection of that source that shows the same level is accepted by itself

guards.name: CI build started while another was running
guards.protects: your configuration items (CIs) from being written by two builds at the same time
guards.action: A CI build was started while another CI build was still running. It did not build beside it: it waited for that build to finish and then built what was left. Nothing is needed. If it happens often, something starts the CI build a second time while it runs -- for example a job run by hand while the pipeline runs.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event. The second CI build still waits for the first one, because two builds never write the CIs at the same time.
guards.what: A CI build was started while another CI build was still running, so it waited for that build to finish and then built what was left.
guards.why: This check tells when two CI builds are asked for at the same time. Two builds side by side would write the same CIs, links and identity records at once, so only one builds at a time. {detail|A second CI build was started while one was running.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: it is information only. Nothing is held -- the second build ran by itself when the first one had finished.
guards.consequence: Nothing is lost: the second build waited and then built what was left, so the CIs are up to date. That run took longer than usual by the time it waited.
steps: Nothing is needed if it happens rarely.
If it happens often, check what starts the CI build while it runs (Operations > Jobs): a job run by hand, or a job on its own schedule beside the pipeline.
guards.neverReleasable: information only: the second build waited and then ran by itself; there is nothing held

guards.name: Data sync: collection of an unfinished run
guards.protects: the collections shown in the Pro web app
guards.action: Some Risk Analysis collections were not loaded into the Pro database because the run that produced them is not known to be complete. Nothing is lost: they are kept and tried again on the next data sync, and an Admin can load one anyway, marked partial, in Operations > Guards (safety checks). If this repeats, check the Risk Analysis Detailed runs.
guards.whenOff: Off: the step goes on as if the check had not tripped -- a collection whose Risk Analysis run did not finish completely is loaded anyway and MARKED PARTIAL in the web app.
guards.what: {v:collectionsHeld|Some} Risk Analysis collection(s) were not loaded into the web app.
guards.why: This check stops results of a Risk Analysis run that did not finish from being shown as complete: findings missing from it would look resolved. {detail|The Risk Analysis run that produced them did not finish completely.}
guards.ifRelease: The collection is loaded into the web app once and marked partial wherever it is shown. Findings missing from it stay unknown, not resolved.
guards.consequence: Nothing is lost: the results ({v:rowsHeld} findings) are kept and can be loaded. [The web app keeps showing the newest complete collection ({latest}) until then.] Pages and trends miss these collections until they are loaded.
steps: Open the Risk Analysis run health to see which part of the run was incomplete.
If the missing part does not matter to you, a SuperAdmin releases the collection with Release in "Held now" at the top of the Guards page.
Otherwise do nothing: the next complete Risk Analysis run is loaded as normal.

guards.name: Data sync: rows without their key
guards.protects: the days shown in the Pro web app and its trends
guards.action: Risk Analysis data arrived without its key columns (its finding ids, or its collection time), so it was not loaded as a day. That day is missing until a complete Risk Analysis run arrives. Check the Risk Analysis Detailed run of that time: its run health says why its data was incomplete.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail. The step itself still stops, because rows without their finding id or collection time cannot be placed in a day.
guards.what: Risk Analysis data was not loaded as a day, because it arrived without its key columns.
guards.why: This check stops rows that cannot be placed in a day from mixing up your history and trends. {detail|The Risk Analysis run delivered rows without their finding ids or their collection time.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: rows without their finding id or collection time are never loaded.
guards.consequence: That run is missing from the web app's history and trends; the collections before and after it are shown as normal. [The newest collection in the web app is {latest}.] This event repeats on every data sync until those rows are older than the look-back window (3 days by default).
steps: Open the Risk Analysis run health of that time to see why its data was incomplete.
Fix the cause: a later complete run is loaded as normal.
Acknowledge this event once you have read it: repeats of exactly this event are hidden too.
guards.neverReleasable: its rows have no key columns (ConfigurationId / CollectionTime): rows without keys are never loaded, released or not

guards.name: Data sync: findings an asset kind filter cannot show
guards.protects: the asset kind filters of the Pro web app
guards.action: Findings of an asset kind were loaded, but their assets were stored without that kind (or without any kind), so the web app's asset kind filter cannot show them. The findings themselves are loaded and counted under All. Check the profiling run of that kind (for example the Azure collector) and the data sync log; if it repeats, contact Invardia support.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail when a loaded collection has findings of an asset kind that no asset of that kind carries; the findings are loaded as before.
guards.what: Some findings are loaded, but the asset kind filter cannot show them.
guards.why: This check warns you that a filtered page shows fewer findings than there are. {detail|Their assets were stored without the asset kind the findings belong to.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: nothing is held. The findings are already loaded; the check only warns.
guards.consequence: The findings are in the web app and counted under All, but a page filtered on that asset kind shows fewer findings (or none) until the assets carry their kind again.
steps: Open the data sync run log of that time to see which kind and how many assets.
Check the collection run of that kind (for example Azure): the next data sync stores the kind again once the collection carries it.
If it repeats, contact Invardia support.
guards.neverReleasable: the collection is already loaded; the guard warns that a kind filter cannot show some of its findings -- review it, there is nothing held

guards.name: Data sync: collection not read in full
guards.protects: the collections shown in the Pro web app
guards.action: A collection could not be read or written in full, so it was not loaded. Nothing is lost: the full collection is tried again on the next data sync. If this repeats, contact Invardia support.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail. The step itself still stops, because a collection that could not be read or written in full is not loaded.
guards.what: A Risk Analysis collection could not be read or written in full, so it was not loaded.
guards.why: This check stops half a collection from being shown as the whole one. {detail|The read from Log Analytics or the write to the database stopped part way.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: a collection read only in part is never loaded as complete. The next data sync reads it again.
guards.consequence: Nothing is lost: the full collection is tried again on the next data sync.
steps: Nothing is needed if it happens once.
If it repeats, contact Invardia support.
guards.neverReleasable: fewer rows were read than the run wrote; the next sync reads it again -- a short read is never loaded as complete

guards.name: Risk Analysis: far fewer findings
guards.protects: the completeness of your Risk Analysis reports
guards.action: One or more reports produced far fewer findings than the previous run. Either the findings were really fixed, or a query stopped matching. Compare the listed reports with the previous run before trusting this export.
guards.whenOff: Off: the step goes on as if the check had not tripped -- a report with far fewer findings than the previous run no longer makes the run partial (a failed query or a missing result still does).
guards.what: {v:reports|Some} Risk Analysis report(s) produced far fewer findings than the previous run.
guards.why: This check warns you before you trust a report that may be missing findings: either the findings were really fixed, or a query stopped matching. {detail|The reports produced far fewer findings than the previous run.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: nothing is held. The reports were delivered; the check only warns.
guards.consequence: The reports were delivered as they are. If a query stopped matching, the missing findings are unknown, not resolved.
steps: Compare the listed reports with the previous run.
If the drop is not real, check the report's query and the data it reads before trusting this export.
guards.neverReleasable: the report is already produced; the guard warns that it lost rows -- review the run, there is nothing held

guards.name: Risk Analysis: far more buckets than usual
guards.protects: the speed and correctness of your Risk Analysis reports
guards.action: One or more reports needed far more buckets (query slices) than usual. That usually means the report's query or the data it reads changed in a way that needs a look. The run completed.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event when a report needs far more buckets than usual; the run itself is unchanged.
guards.what: {v:reports|Some} Risk Analysis report(s) needed far more buckets than usual (largest {v:largest|unknown}).
guards.why: This check warns you that a report whose bucket count jumps to 4 times its usual count, or above 256, points at a query or data problem rather than normal growth. {detail|A report needed far more buckets than usual.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: nothing is held. The reports were delivered; the check only warns.
guards.consequence: The reports were delivered as they are, but the listed reports took far more queries than usual, so the run was slower.
steps: Open Operations > Risk Analysis query splitting and look at the listed reports.
If the count is wrong, reset that report there: the next run sizes it again.
guards.neverReleasable: the reports are already produced; the guard warns about their bucket counts -- review them, there is nothing held

guards.name: Risk Analysis: column emptied
guards.protects: the completeness of your Risk Analysis reports
guards.action: One or more report columns are empty (or gone) while they had values in the previous run. Check the listed columns before trusting this export.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail when a report column lost its content; the report itself is unchanged.
guards.what: {v:columns|Some} report column(s) are empty or gone, while they had values in the previous run.
guards.why: This check warns you that filters and scores reading those columns may be wrong for this run. {detail|A source stopped delivering a value, or a column was renamed.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: nothing is held. The reports were delivered; the check only warns.
guards.consequence: The reports were delivered with these columns empty; filters and scores that read them may be wrong for this run.
steps: Check the listed columns before trusting this export.
If a source stopped delivering, fix its permission or setting: the next run fills the columns again.
guards.neverReleasable: the report is already produced; the guard warns that a column is empty -- review the run, there is nothing held

guards.name: Log Analytics: rows not accepted
guards.protects: the results written to your Log Analytics workspace
guards.action: Not every row of a result was accepted by Log Analytics, so the run was stopped instead of reporting a partial result as complete. Nothing is closed or retired on the strength of it; the next run writes the full result again. If this repeats, contact Invardia support.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail. The step itself still stops, because the rows Log Analytics did not accept are not there.
guards.what: The run was stopped, because Log Analytics did not accept every row of a result.
guards.why: This check stops later steps from closing or retiring anything because of a result that is only partly stored. {detail|Part of the result was refused while it was written to your Log Analytics workspace.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: the rows that were not accepted are not there. The next run sends them again.
guards.consequence: Nothing is closed or retired on the strength of a partial result; the next run writes the full result again.
steps: Nothing is needed if it happens once.
If it repeats, contact Invardia support.
guards.neverReleasable: Log Analytics stored fewer rows than were sent; the next run sends them again -- nothing is held

guards.name: Database change that could remove data
guards.protects: your SecurityInsight database
guards.action: A database change was refused because it is not approved for this install, or because it could remove data. Nothing was applied. Contact Invardia support with the message from setup.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail. The step itself still stops, because a database change that could remove data is never applied automatically.
guards.what: A database change was refused, and nothing was applied.
guards.why: This check protects your data: SecurityInsight only adds to its database, and never applies a change that could remove data. {detail|The change is not approved for this install, or it could remove data.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: a change that could remove data is never applied, whoever asks.
guards.consequence: Your SecurityInsight database is unchanged; features that need the change wait until it is applied.
steps: Contact Invardia support with the message from setup.
guards.neverReleasable: SecurityInsight applies additive schema only; a schema that drops or rewrites data is never applied, whoever asks (integrity)

guards.name: Update: database update failed
guards.protects: your SecurityInsight installation from running a new version on an old database
guards.action: An update stopped before it changed anything, because the new version's database changes could not be applied. Your installation keeps running the version it ran before. Make sure the updater's identity has the database rights the release notes name, then start the updater again; if it repeats, contact Invardia support with the message from the update.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail. The step itself still stops, because the database update failed.
guards.what: An update stopped before rolling out the new version, because its database changes could not be applied.
guards.why: This check stops a new version from running on an old database, which could break jobs or the web app. {detail|The database refused a change the new version needs, or the updater could not sign in to it.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: new code never runs on an old database. The update waits until the database change applies.
guards.consequence: Nothing changed: every job and the web app keep running the version they ran before. The update is tried again on the next updater run.
steps: Check that the updater's identity has the database rights the release notes name.
Start the updater again (or wait for its next daily run).
If it repeats, contact Invardia support with the message from the update.
guards.neverReleasable: new code never runs on an old schema; the update waits until the schema applies (integrity)

guards.name: Licence not valid
guards.protects: the SecurityInsight Pro features
guards.action: The SecurityInsight Pro licence does not verify (it has expired or is not valid for this install), so the Pro jobs did not run. Install a current licence, or contact Invardia.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail. The step itself still stops, because the licence, not this switch, decides which Pro features run.
guards.what: The SecurityInsight Pro jobs did not run, because the licence does not verify.
guards.why: This check pauses the Pro features while the licence does not verify: the licence decides which Pro features run. {detail|The licence has expired or is not valid for this install.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: a licence is checked, never released. Install a valid licence.
guards.consequence: The Pro features are paused; no data is removed. They start again as soon as a valid licence is installed.
steps: Install a current licence, or contact Invardia.
guards.neverReleasable: a licence is checked, never released: install a valid licence (integrity)

guards.name: Licence grace period
guards.protects: the SecurityInsight Pro features
guards.action: The SecurityInsight Pro licence is in its grace period. Everything keeps running for now; renew the licence before the grace period ends.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail during the licence grace period; everything keeps running.
guards.what: The SecurityInsight Pro licence is in its grace period.
guards.why: This check tells you in time that the licence must be renewed. {detail|The licence has expired; the grace period keeps everything running for now.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: a licence is checked, never released. Renew it before the grace period ends.
guards.consequence: Everything keeps running for now. When the grace period ends, the Pro jobs stop until the licence is renewed.
steps: Renew the licence before the grace period ends.
guards.neverReleasable: a licence is checked, never released: renew the licence before the grace period ends (integrity)

guards.name: Audit trail retention setting
guards.protects: the audit trail
guards.action: The audit trail retention setting (SI_Pro_AuditRetentionMonths) is not a whole number of at least 13 months, so nothing was removed. Correct the setting on the Settings page.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail. The step itself still stops, because the retention setting is not valid.
guards.what: No audit trail entries were removed, because the retention setting is not valid.
guards.why: This check protects your audit trail: it is kept at least 13 months, so entries are never removed on a setting that is not valid. {detail|The audit retention setting is not a whole number of at least 13 months.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: the audit trail is kept at least 13 months.
guards.consequence: Nothing is lost: the whole audit trail is kept until the setting is corrected.
steps: Correct the audit trail retention on the Settings page (a whole number of months, at least 13).
guards.neverReleasable: the audit trail is kept at least 13 months; a retention guard is never released (integrity of the evidence)

guards.name: Bulk exemption limit
guards.protects: your findings from being exempted in bulk by mistake
guards.action: A request to exempt or change many findings at once was refused (no narrowing filter, or more findings than the limit allows). Nothing was changed. If the request was intended, narrow the filter or raise SIWeb_Exemption_BulkMax deliberately.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail. The request itself is still refused, because a whole collection is never exempted in one go -- raise the limit instead (Settings > Exemptions: Most findings in one bulk exemption request, up to 2,000).
guards.what: A request to exempt or change many findings at once was refused.
guards.why: This check stops many findings from being exempted in one click by mistake. {detail|The request had no narrowing filter, or more findings than the limit allows.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: narrow the selection and send the request again, or raise the limit.
guards.consequence: Nothing was changed: every finding keeps its state.
steps: If the request was intended, narrow the filter and send it again.
Or raise the limit on purpose (Settings > Exemptions: most findings in one bulk exemption request).
guards.neverReleasable: a bulk exemption over the limit is refused by design; narrow the selection instead
guards.limitsInfo: The limit is set under Settings > Exemptions (most findings in one bulk exemption request). A higher limit lets bigger requests through in one click.

guards.name: Daily flow: start held for the previous run
guards.protects: the order of the daily jobs
guards.action: A scheduled start of the daily job flow was held because the previous run was still running; it ran once as soon as that run finished. Nothing is needed if it happens rarely.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail; the daily flow still waits for its previous run.
guards.what: A scheduled start of the daily job flow was missed: it started later than its time, and not only because the previous run was still going.
guards.why: This check tells when the daily jobs do not start at their time. A start that only waits for a long previous run is normal and is not reported; any other late start is. {detail|The start was not made at its scheduled time.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: it is information only. The missed start already ran once, late.
guards.consequence: Nothing is lost: the missed start ran once, late, so the data was refreshed later than scheduled.
steps: Nothing is needed if it happens rarely.
If it happens again, check that the pipeline's job is switched on and that nothing held it at its start time, for example an update that took long.
guards.neverReleasable: information only: the pipeline made a missed start late; there is nothing held

guards.name: Daily flow: jobs skipped
guards.protects: the jobs that depend on an earlier job
guards.action: One or more jobs in the daily flow were skipped because a job they need did not succeed. Fix the failed job (see Operations > Jobs), then use Re-run from here.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail; jobs that need a failed job are still skipped.
guards.what: {held|Some} job(s) in the daily flow were skipped, because a job they need did not succeed.
guards.why: This check stops jobs from working on missing or old data from a job that failed. {detail|An earlier job in the flow failed.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: the skipped jobs need the failed job's data. Fix the failed job and run again.
guards.consequence: The skipped jobs did not update their data this time: their pages show the previous run until the next successful run. Nothing is lost.
steps: Fix the failed job (see Operations > Jobs).
Use Re-run from here, or wait for the next scheduled run.
guards.neverReleasable: the step did not run because its input was missing; the next run resolves it -- there is nothing held

guards.name: Daily flow: job did not start
guards.protects: the jobs of the daily flow
guards.action: A job in the daily flow could not start: its container stopped before SecurityInsight ran (an Azure platform problem). It was started again automatically and did not start that time either. Check the job's executions in Operations > Jobs; when Azure is healthy again, use Re-run from here. If it happens again, contact Invardia support.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail; a job that does not start is still not run.
guards.what: A job in the daily flow could not start, also not when it was started again.
guards.why: This check tells you that a job did not run, so you do not trust data that was not updated. {detail|Its container stopped before SecurityInsight ran (an Azure platform problem).}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: nothing is held. Run the job again when Azure is healthy.
guards.consequence: That job's data was not updated this time, and jobs that need it may have been skipped. Nothing else is lost.
steps: Check the job's runs in Operations > Jobs.
When Azure is healthy again, use Re-run from here.
If it happens again, contact Invardia support.
guards.neverReleasable: the job could not be started; re-run it on the Jobs page -- there is nothing held

guards.name: Daily flow: job interrupted
guards.protects: the jobs that depend on an earlier job
guards.action: A job in the daily flow was interrupted and was not started again automatically. Check Operations > Jobs and use Re-run from here when ready.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail; an interrupted job is still not started again.
guards.what: {held|Some} job(s) in the daily flow were interrupted and not started again automatically.
guards.why: This check tells you that a job stopped part way, so its data and the jobs that need it are not up to date. {detail|The job stopped part way, for example because its container was restarted.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: nothing is held. Run the job again on the Jobs page.
guards.consequence: Those jobs did not update their data this time, and jobs that need them wait.
steps: Check Operations > Jobs.
Use Re-run from here when ready.
guards.neverReleasable: the job was interrupted; re-run it on the Jobs page -- there is nothing held

guards.name: Job started while still running
guards.protects: a job from running twice at the same time
guards.action: A job was started while its previous run was still running, so the new run did nothing. If this happens every day, the job takes longer than its schedule allows: start it less often.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail. The step itself still stops, because two runs of one job never run at the same time.
guards.what: A job was started while its previous run was still running, so the new run did nothing.
guards.why: This check stops one job from running twice at the same time, which would write the same data twice. {detail|The previous run of the job had not finished.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: a job never runs twice at the same time.
guards.consequence: Nothing is lost: the running job finishes its work.
steps: Nothing is needed if it happens rarely.
If it happens every day, the job takes longer than its schedule allows: start it less often.
guards.neverReleasable: a job never runs twice at the same time (SCHED-1); the skipped start runs when the previous run finishes

guards.name: Job stuck on throttling
guards.protects: the data of a job that Microsoft keeps throttling
guards.action: Microsoft has throttled this job on every run for a long time, so it has not completed since. Throttling on its own is normal and is never mailed; this mail means the job cannot catch up by itself. Check whether other tools use the same Microsoft services heavily at the same time, or run the job at a quieter time. The alert clears by itself after the next run that completes.
guards.whenOff: Off: no event and no mail when a job is stuck on throttling. Throttled runs are still shown as throttled on the Jobs and Run health pages.
guards.what: A job has not completed for a long time, because Microsoft throttled every run of it.
guards.why: This check tells you when a job has not been able to complete for a long stretch, so you do not rely on data that is getting old. Throttling on its own is normal and is not reported. {detail|Every run of the job was throttled by Microsoft.}
guards.ifRelease: This check cannot be released: nothing is held. The next run that completes clears it.
guards.consequence: The job's data was not updated while it was stuck. The previous results stay in place, and findings it could not check are unknown, not resolved. Nothing is lost.
steps: Check the job on the Jobs page (Operations > Jobs).
If other tools use the same Microsoft services heavily, run this job at a quieter time.
If it stays stuck, contact Invardia support.
guards.neverReleasable: nothing is held; the alert clears by itself after the next run that completes
